This Contempt petition has been filed under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act read with Article 215 of the Constitution of India to initiate contempt proceedings against respondents for non-complaince of order dated 20-10-2016 passed in WPC No. 1021/2016 (Pushpa Bai Agrawal and anr. Vs. State of Chhattisgarh and ors.).
3. Brief facts of the case as projected in the WP(C) No. 1021/2016 are that

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the petitioners who claim to be owners being title holder of disputed land bearing Khasra No. 628/1, 628/3 and 629 total area 4.320 hectare and 1.530 hectare respectively situated at Patwari Halka No. 00005 at village Amleshwar, Revenue Circle Bhilai, Tahsil Patan, Distt. Durg and
they are in possession of the same since last about 35 years.

It was alleged that respondents in the name of a project being developed by the government, without following the acquisition procedure and due process of law and without even paying contingent part for payment of any compensation, have made some construction on their land.
It was further submitted that the respondents are constructing road on their lands without serving any notice to them.
It was also submitted that the petitioners made various requests and representations before the respondents, but the same has not been considered by the respondents/authorities.
Therefore, they filed the said writ petition.

4. Learned Single Judge vide order dated 20-10-2016 passed in W.P.C. No. 1021/2016 disposed of the writ petition and passed following order :-
"Heard.
2.

The petitioners have preferred this writ petition seeking a direction to the respondents to initiate proceedings for acquiring their land, which has been used for construction of park, bathing ghat, cemented pathway and embankment.

3. Perusal of the documents filed with the writ petition and with the return would demonstrate that there is some dispute as to whether any area has been used for such construction and if any area has been used, what is the exact extent of such area.

4. Be that as it may, the ends of justice would be served, if the respondent Department, which has undertaken the construction work, is directed to carry out the demarcation of the land to ascertain as to what exact area owned by the petitioners has been used in the construction and thereafter, to proceed for acquisition of land used in such construction.

5. Let the demarcation be carried out within a period of 02 months and thereafter,
the acquisition proceedings be initiated without further delay.
The entire acquisition proceedings shall be completed within a period of 06 months from the date of demarcation.
6. The writ petition is accordingly disposed of."

sentences.text: Now the petitioners have filed instant contempt petition for initiation of contempt proceedings against the respondents for non-compliance of above order.

6. Since there is dispute about the area of land of the petitioners used by the respondents, this Court vide order dated 12-9-2019 appointed Mr. Avinash K. Mishra, Advocate as Commissioner to measure the subject area with the assistance of Revenue Inspector and Tahsildar of the concerned area, Shri Piyush Raj Verma, Atchitect of Raipur and one Engineer not below the rank of Assistant Engineer in the Department of Irrigation.
The Commissioner's report was filed.
Being aggrieved by the report of the Commissioner, the petitioners have filed a Writ Petition (C) No. 923/2019 before this Court, which is still pending consideration.

7. It has been argued by Mr. Y.C. Sharma, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Sachin Nidhi,
learned counsel for the petitioners that present contempt petition has been filed for non-compliance of order dated 20-10-2016 passed by learned Single Judge in W.P.C. No. 1021/2016.
He further submits that now the order has been partially complied with, but not fully complied with.

Hence,
this petition at this stage cannot be disposed of.

8. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondents submits that order of learned Single Judge was to carry out the demarcation of the land and to initiate the acquisition proceedings.
Both the directions have been complied with by the respondents as demarcation of land has been done and compensation has also been given to the petitioners.

It is further submitted that if petitioners are unsatisfied with the demarcation report submitted by the Commissioner,
which is subject matter of WPC No. 923/2019 and pending consideration before learned Single Judge of this Court, then they may raise their grievance before learned Single Judge and therefore,
their submission is that as the report of Court Commissioner is still to be examined by the learned Single Judge, hence present contempt petition may be disposed of.
If petitioners would have any grievance for non- compliance of any order of this Court, they may be at liberty to approach this Court again.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and in view of the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, there has been compliance of the order dated 20-10-2016 passed by learned Single Judge in W.P.C. No. 1021/2016 of making demarcation of land and initiation of acquisition proceedings.

If the petitioners have any grievance with regard to the demarcation report or amount of compensation given in acquisition proceedings, they may raise their contention before learned Single Judge, as the same is subject matter of WPC No. 923/2019 which is pending consideration.
10. In view of above observations, the instant contempt petition is disposed of.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (N. K. Chandravanshi) (Ramesh Sinha)
